# Norman Douglas & Wilson

- [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) — Commands — [Wilson](../character/wilson.md) — housekeeper · since v5  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XVI. TIT FOR TAT P27](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0027)</sub>

## Shared scenes

> [Faith](../character/faith.md) walks down the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) with [Walter](../character/walter.md), who suffers from a toothache and worries about his inability to confront bullies like [Dan Reese](../character/dan-reese.md), who hurls insults at [Faith](../character/faith.md) as they pass. [Faith](../character/faith.md) then visits [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) to persuade him to return to church and pay his salary, but she is initially intimidated and retreats after he shouts at her. Furious at his insults, [Faith](../character/faith.md) returns to confront him directly; impressed by her fiery spirit, Norman apologizes, agrees to return to church, and invites her to sit for supper.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XVI. TIT FOR TAT

> [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) admires Faith's spirited confrontation and convinces her to share a meal with him. He agrees to contribute to the church salary and attend services once a month, provided [Faith](../character/faith.md) accepts his nickname 'Red Rose' for her and hears his unorthodox views. Afterwards, Norman drives [Faith](../character/faith.md) home with a buggy full of gifts, leaving her relieved that her father's position in the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) is secure.
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XVI. TIT FOR TAT

> [Mary Vance](../character/mary-vance.md) meets [Faith](../character/faith.md), [Una](../character/una-meredith.md), [Nan](../character/nan-blythe.md), and [Di](../character/di.md) in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) while on her way to [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside), proudly showing off her new winter clothes. [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) feels envious and self-conscious about her shabby garments, but eventually softens toward Mary after a tense interaction. When Mary mentions that [Aunt Martha](../character/aunt-martha.md) killed a rooster for dinner, [Faith](../character/faith.md) panics and races home to save her pet rooster, [Adam](../character/adam.md).
>
> — v5 · CHAPTER XVIII. MARY BRINGS EVIL TIDINGS
